sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the agreement] Russia and Ukraine agreed a large-scale prisoner exchange after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi (The National; confirmed by Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky and by US envoy Jared Kushner). [VERIFIED FACT -- the Moscow trip] Kushner said he and Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday Nov 12 to meet President Vladimir Putin 'to go over what was discussed in Abu Dhabi and try to make more progress', then meet President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (The National; Kurdistan24 specifies the Zelenskyy meeting is in Dublin, where the European Political Community summit convenes Nov 12). [VERIFIED FACT -- the format] The trilateral talks lasted just under two hours on day 2 (day 1: ~4.5 hours); a round of talks with European representatives then began (Interfax-Ukraine, source close to the Ukrainian team). [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the number, NOT final] An exchange of 1,000-for-1,000 'or more' was agreed in the near future per an Interfax-Ukraine source; Zelenskyy said day 1 discussed 1,000-for-1,000 or 1,500-for-1,500. Kushner: 'we agreed we'll have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners and we'll finalise the numbers tomorrow.' The number is therefore NOT a confirmed agreed figure. [VERIFIED FACT -- progress claimed on monitoring] Kushner: 'We made good progress on understanding how to deconflict and how to monitor the ceasefire.' No ceasefire was agreed. [CONTEXT -- the war went on during the talks] Russia struck six large electricity substations in Ukraine's four central regions on Wednesday plus railways in the east and centre (Ukrainian PM Sergii Koretskyi, via The National). [CONTEXT -- the 15:00 scan closed with 'no outcome by scan close'; the TASS conclusion post (12:19 Kyiv = 14:19 ) and the Kushner presser landed after that close, so the outcome is new to this scan.]
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: The National (T2), TASS (T3 STATE RU), Xinhua (T3 STATE CN). Kyiv Post, Interfax-Ukraine, APA and Kurdistan24 also carried the outcome but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration. Passes the >=2-family gate on the three tiered families alone.
sections.what_disputed: No ceasefire agreed; Russian FM Lavrov explicitly rejected European ceasefire demands (CBS, via The Leadsman summary). Territory unresolved: Russia demands the full Donbas including ground it has not captured; Zelenskyy says territory is a matter for leaders. Medinsky dismissed EU participation ('We haven't spoken with them. We don't really understand their status here'). Russia struck six large substations plus railways in Ukraine on Wednesday while the talks ran. No date was set for a third session. The Leadsman notes the two days produced a process confirmation, a humanitarian commitment and a rhetorical formulation -- not a settlement.
sections.why_matters: First concrete outcome of the first US-mediated talks since February: the biggest prisoner release of the war is agreed -- but the numbers are not final, there is no ceasefire, and Russia hit six substations the same day. Kushner flies to Putin tomorrow.

totw_analysis: Our read: First concrete outcome of the first US-mediated talks since February: the biggest prisoner release of the war is agreed -- but the numbers are not final, there is no ceasefire, and Russia hit six substations the same day. Kushner flies to Putin tomorrow. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Prisoner swap first or ceasefire first? Kyiv and Washington sell the exchange as a 'good first step'; the fault line is whether a swap with no ceasefire and no territory movement is real progress or a pressure valve that lets the war grind on.
